elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer may solicit, hire, or employ Vendor employees without restriction." The prohibition ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is gone, so no non-solicit, no-hire or no-employ obligation binds the Customer anywhere in the cited text, and § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made "no ... no-hire commitment" is now consistent.

Condition inapplicable: after the edit no non-solicitation restriction binds either Party, so there is no asymmetry to cure; the preferred outcome (no restriction on Customer) is more protective than a mutual restriction.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no restriction survives in § 12.4, so no scope limitation is needed. (The deterministic scope/duration checks fail only because there is no longer any restriction text to measure.)

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: the 24-month tail was deleted along with the restriction; the "duration ≤ 12 months — number not found" check reflects the absence of any duration, not an unbounded one.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no restriction remains to carve out from, and retained § 12.3 independently confirms Customer may hire "any person who responds to general recruitment." The failing carve-out regex is therefore not a defect on this path.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: with § 12.4 converted to a permission, unsolicited approaches are unrestricted; the offending "regardless of how the employee applies" language was removed.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The no-hire component ("hire, or employ") is deleted; § 12.4 now affirmatively permits Customer to "solicit, hire, or employ Vendor employees", consistent with § 12.3.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the sole preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment — § 12.4 no longer imposes any solicitation, hiring or employment restriction on Customer.

The two failing deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are artefacts of the preferred path: there is no surviving restriction to date-limit or carve out from, so they do not indicate a defect. The minimality and element-coverage gates pass.

Minimal: only the offending § 12.4 is touched; favourable § 12.3 is retained verbatim and no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra covenant is added. Note (rationale-level only, not a defect): the affirmative "may solicit, hire, or employ ... without restriction" partially restates § 12.3's no-no-hire acknowledgement, and striking § 12.4 outright would be marginally cleaner.

Preserves intent: no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, and the edit removes rather than creates a contradiction with § 12.3; unrelated allocation, timing and commercial mechanics are untouched.

Deviation classification is correct: the original clause sat in walk-away territory (express no-hire, all Vendor employees, term plus 24 months, "regardless of how the employee applies"), failing every fallback element, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale-only note.

Fallback marked satisfied only vacuously (no restriction exists on either side); the comment correctly offers the mutual, 12-month, involvement-limited non-solicit with carve-outs as the negotiating fallback.
